text: SUPERVISOR — addition to your TWIGRESTORE undo slice: KEYBOARD BINDINGS. User verbatim: "and there is nno control z or other keyboard fn" — the workbench editors have undo/redo as BUTTONS only; no ctrl+z, no standard keyboard functions at all. Wire the standard editor keys at the workbench SHELL level so they work in every source and lens uniformly: ctrl+z -> undo, ctrl+shift+z (and ctrl+y) -> redo, ctrl+s -> save (the same save the button does). They dispatch into the same undo machinery you are building (stroke-granular) — one undo system, two entry points (button + key). Respect focus rules: keys must not fire while a text input is focused except their native text behavior. Discoverable: tooltips on the existing buttons show the shortcut. Test at the consumption layer: stroke -> ctrl+z -> exactly that stroke gone, in BOTH a character paint lens and the items sculpt lens. The user's muscle memory working is the PASS.
resolution: Keyboard bindings are committed for review. The Workbench shell remains the ctrl+z/ctrl+y/ctrl+shift+z/ctrl+s owner, character paint routes save/undo/redo to the live paint bench actions, embedded paint hotkeys are disabled under the shell, and the duplicate per-stage handlers were removed so keyboard entry and button entry hit the same stroke-granular undo machinery.
